label: I q.19 a.3: Willing an end necessitates willing only indispensable means to it
interpretation: The necessity in this reading follows from willing the end. Aquinas contrasts food for preserving life or a ship for crossing the sea with a horse for a journey that can also be made on foot. In God's case, his goodness can be had without creatures. Necessity on the supposition that God wills a creature follows from the immutability of that willing.
attribution: The passage states that willing an end necessitates willing a particular means to it only if that end cannot be had without that means, which is the premise.
